Robust, Self-Funded Pipeline ​ BP-205 (Orexin-2 receptor agonist) ​ BP-205 MAD Study Design and Preliminary Results ● 14-day double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study that evaluated once-daily doses of BP-205 at 0.1 mg, 0.6 mg, 1 mg, and 3 mg across six cohorts (4 male and 2 female); a total of 94 healthy volunteers participated in this study ● BP-205 was rapidly absorbed, with a mean T (max) of approximately 60 minutes (range 30 to 90 minutes) supportive of the potential for rapid onset of efficacy ● The mean effective half-life (T 1/2 ) after 14-day repeat dosing was observed to be approximately 29 hours; no clinically meaningful change compared to the half-life in the SAD study and supportive of once-daily dosing ● BP-205 was generally well tolerated across all doses evaluated: headache was the most common adverse event occurring in approximately 25% of participants ● On-target adverse events of insomnia were reported in less than 20% of participants at all doses evaluated, were mild in severity and did not lead to discontinuation ● On-target adverse events of urinary frequency and urgency were reported in less than 20% of participants at the 1mg and 3mg doses only; these events were mild in severity and did not lead to discontinuation ● No liver or visual adverse events were reported, and no clinically significant cardiovascular events or EKG abnormalities were recorded ● There were no serious or severe adverse events ● The complete MAD study results will be presented at an upcoming medical meeting ● Next steps in BP-205 development: o Phase 1b study in sleep-deprived healthy volunteers initiated in Q3 in the US; data expected in Q1 2027 o Expect to initiate Phase 2 studies to evaluate multiple CNS indications by mid-2027 ​ ​ ​ ​ ​
